headline: pki.smime.verify / decrypt can now recognize a legacy (RFC 8551) header-protected message -- opt in with `legacyHeaderProtection` and the real headers of an older `message/rfc822`-wrapped message are surfaced instead of read as unprotected.
summary: S/MIME header protection (RFC 9788) gains inbound support for the legacy RFC 8551 scheme (RFC 9788 sec. 4.10): a message whose signed/encrypted payload is a bare `message/rfc822` object carrying the real headers, with no `hp=` parameter. Pass `opts.legacyHeaderProtection: true` to `pki.smime.verify` or `pki.smime.decrypt` and a legacy message that meets the RFC 9788 sec. 4.10.1 identification test has its inner headers surfaced as `protectedHeaders`, with `headerProtection.legacy: true`, the mode inferred from the envelope (`clear` for signed, `cipher` for encrypted), and -- for an encrypted message -- the confidential set derived from the actual visible outer headers. Detection is off by default and fail-safe: it runs only after the signature or authenticated-decryption verdict succeeds, requires every one of the four identification conditions, and never mis-surfaces an ordinary forwarded `message/rfc822`, a nested crypto layer, or a message that declares `hp=` on its inner part -- anything not precisely identified stays `protectedHeaders: null`, exactly as before. The `legacy` flag marks the weaker, structurally inferred provenance so it is never confused with a cryptographically declared `hp=` set. No wire format changes; sending remains unchanged (RFC 9788 forbids generating the legacy wrap).

Added: pki.smime.verify and pki.smime.decrypt accept opts.legacyHeaderProtection: true to detect and surface a legacy RFC 8551 header-protected message (RFC 9788 sec. 4.10) -- a signed or encrypted payload that is a bare message/rfc822 wrap with no hp= parameter. On a precise match the inner message's Non-Structural headers become protectedHeaders, headerProtection.legacy is true, the mode is inferred from the envelope (clear signed / cipher encrypted), and an encrypted message's confidential set is computed against the visible outer headers. RFC 9788 sec. 4.10.1 / sec. 4.10.2, RFC 8551.

headerProtection now carries a legacy boolean on every verify / decrypt result: true only for a legacy message recovered via legacyHeaderProtection, false for a standard hp= set and for a non-protected message -- so a structurally inferred set is never conflated with a cryptographically declared one.
Changed: Detection is opt-in and fail-safe. Without legacyHeaderProtection the behavior is unchanged: a legacy-form message reads as protectedHeaders: null (never mis-authenticated). With the option set, a message that is not precisely identified -- an ordinary forwarded message/rfc822, an inner part that is itself a signed/encrypted layer, or an inner part declaring hp= -- also stays protectedHeaders: null rather than being surfaced. The signed-and-encrypted legacy form (RFC 9788 Appendix C.3.17) surfaces as clear via the caller's re-verify step, a documented limitation of the non-recursive layered API.
